h1: TR Guesthouse — a budget guesthouse in the heart of New Sukhothai that's great value and walkable to everything
intro: If you're coming to Sukhothai on a budget but still want a clean room, friendly hosts and a spot right in the centre of the New City, TR Guesthouse is a name backpackers have recommended for years. It sits in the New City near the Yom River, a few minutes' walk from the night market, eateries and the songthaew pick-up for the Historical Park. You can choose between hotel rooms in the front building or garden bungalows at the back, with comfy beds, mosquito nets and hot-water bathrooms. From approx THB 600/night. TripAdvisor rates it 4.3/5 from 520 reviews, among the top-ranked guesthouses in Sukhothai.

body.html: TR Guesthouse sits on Pravet Nakorn Road in New Sukhothai, near the Yom River. The big draw of this location is that you can walk to the night market, eateries, convenience stores and the songthaew pick-up for the Historical Park in just a few minutes — unlike the old-town stays, which are peaceful but mean driving out to find food. The Sukhothai Historical Park is about 12 km away; you can take a songthaew or hire a motorbike to get there easily. It's a good fit for travellers who want the convenience of the New City on a budget.

There are around 20 rooms here, split into two styles — hotel rooms in the front building and garden bungalows at the back. The bungalows are the favourite for many travellers: comfy queen beds, mosquito nets, hardwood floors and a small porch facing the garden. The hotel rooms are standard air-conditioned rooms with a TV, desk and en-suite bathroom with hot water. Every room has free Wi-Fi. Most reviews praise the rooms as clean, the beds as comfortable, and the whole thing as great value for what you pay.

"Clean room, comfy bed for the price, and the owner was so kind — helped arrange a ride to the station and gave us tips on where to go. Step out of the lane and you're at restaurants and the market. Perfect for anyone on a budget."

What keeps TR Guesthouse scoring well is the warmth and helpfulness of the owner and staff. Reviews mention the owner recommending restaurants, arranging rides to the bus station or airport, and sometimes driving guests there in person. There's motorbike and bicycle hire for getting around, laundry service, and inexpensive food and drinks on site. The vibe is family-run — more like staying at a relative's house than a hotel. This is the voice of real reviews behind its TripAdvisor 4.3/5 from 520 reviews and a Booking.com score around 8.8.

There are a few things to know before you book. As a budget guesthouse, the facilities are simple — no pool, gym or resort spa. Breakfast isn't included with every room (there's a Western breakfast you can add), so check when you book. Some reviews mention rooms that get hot because of weak insulation, and service that can be inconsistent at times. And because it's near the Yom River, once or twice a year in the rainy season there can be some flooding at the mouth of the lane — though it doesn't happen often.

In short, TR Guesthouse suits travellers looking for a clean, budget stay in the heart of the New City who value location and a warm welcome over fancy facilities. If you're a backpacker, a budget-minded couple, or someone who wants to walk to restaurants and transport, it's a good fit at this price. But if the heart of your trip is cycling into the ruins first thing in the morning, an old-town hotel gets you there more directly — and if you want a pool and full service, it's worth stepping up to a midrange stay.

A tip from following the reviews here for a while: if you prefer a quieter, more private feel, ask for a garden bungalow at the back rather than a front hotel room. Let the owner know in advance if you'd like a pickup from the station or airport, and book a motorbike ahead if you plan to ride out to the park. During the Loy Krathong / Sukhothai light festival, rooms fill up fast — book several weeks ahead.

faq.q: Where is TR Guesthouse and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's on Pravet Nakorn Road in New Sukhothai, near the Yom River. A few minutes' walk to the night market, eateries, convenience stores and the songthaew pick-up for the Historical Park. The bus station is about a 5-minute drive, and the Sukhothai Historical Park is about 12 km away — reachable by songthaew or motorbike hire.

faq.q: How much does TR Guesthouse cost and what rooms are there?
faq.a: From approx THB 600/night for a Standard Room (air-conditioned hotel room). There's a Garden Bungalow with a mosquito net and porch from around THB 750, and a roomier Superior Room from around THB 900. Prices shift with the season and festivals, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: What's the difference between the bungalows and the hotel rooms?
faq.a: The bungalows are in the back garden — quieter and more private, with a queen bed, mosquito net, hardwood floor and a small porch facing the garden. The hotel rooms are at the front — standard air-conditioned rooms with a TV and hot-water bathroom, closer to the street. Pick the bungalow for a quieter vibe, or the hotel room for easy street access.

faq.q: Staying in the New City vs the Old City of Sukhothai — what's the difference?
faq.a: The New City (where TR Guesthouse is) is convenient for restaurants, markets and the bus station, but it's about 12 km out to the park. The Old City is right by the Historical Park — you can cycle into the ruins first thing — but has fewer restaurants and is quieter. Choose based on whether your trip leans toward convenience or the ruins.

faq.q: Who is TR Guesthouse best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for backpackers, budget-minded couples, or travellers who want a clean stay in the heart of the New City on a budget. It's an easy walk to restaurants and transport, and the owner arranges rides and motorbike hire. It's less suited to anyone who wants a pool, gym or full resort-style service.

faq.q: How far ahead should I book?
faq.a: During high season (November–February) and the Loy Krathong / Sukhothai light festival, rooms fill up fast, so book several weeks ahead. The rest of the year, 1–2 weeks is usually fine. Choose a free-cancellation rate if your plans aren't firm yet.
